The Aging Parent Care Planning Checklist

What to notice, talk about and ask while Mom is still managing at home.

Download PDF

Mom still does most things herself, and you've noticed a few small changes. Nothing has to happen this week. Check what you've looked at, talked about or written down. Anything unchecked is something to get to when there's a good moment, not a verdict about Mom.

Notice

Talk about with Mom

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you notice, talk and ask. It doesn't say what a change means, whether Mom needs more help, or what kind. That's for the people who know her health and her situation. Nothing here is medical, legal, financial or tax advice.

Ready for the next step?

You've looked, talked and listed your questions. The care interview walks you through Mom's situation area by area so nothing important is overlooked, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from

The item marked 1 follows the everyday activities LongTermCare.gov lists. Items marked 2 follow its page on avoiding a fall, which suggests noticing how a person walks, asking about medications and looking over the home. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
